clue.text: Where to see bathyspheres having problems

explanation.surface: A question about where deep-sea diving bells go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathyspheres are diving vessels used far below the ocean surface, and the same phrase is an idiom for being in serious trouble.

clue.text: In a temper, I desert city

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray one's side
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Someone angrily abandons a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a noun but is the verb, giving RAT. ELY is a small English cathedral city, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something while in a temper means doing it angrily, an adverb of manner.

clue.text: Object surfacing during excavations made us rich

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed 'Object surfacing during excavations made us rich (5)': no hidden or reversed run of the words gives DEMUR, and no other parse builds it; the clue appears garbled.
annotationWithheld.clue: Object surfacing during excavations made us rich

clue.text: It's not difficult to preside over 28

parts.note: something not difficult is easy
to chair a meeting is to preside over it

explanation.surface: Chairing a meeting is no hard task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link in this down clue, putting the first piece above the second. 28 refers to the answer to 28 across, a resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair is a comfortable seat where one rests, so it is one kind of spot for repose.

clue.text: A bit pale, not completely

indicators.note: not completely means the word for pale loses its final letter

parts.note: pale means white in colour

explanation.surface: Someone looks slightly pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completely' drops the last letter from WHITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is a tiny amount, as in 'not a whit', so it means a small piece.

clue.text: Radio not adapted for oven cooking

indicators.note: adapted means the letters of the two words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio that has not been modified for use in a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges RADIONOT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori food is cooked in a tandoor, a clay oven from South Asia.

clue.text: Problem concerning transport

parts.note: re means concerning, as in business letters
a bus is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A difficulty with getting about.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture puzzle in which images stand for words is a kind of brain-teaser.

clue.text: Will electromotive force circulate one charged atom?

indicators.note: circulate means the measure of force goes round the next piece

parts.note: electromotive force is measured in volts
I is the Roman numeral one
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A physics question about electromotive force moving a charged particle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a name or a legal document; it is the faculty of choosing. 'circulate' makes the volt unit wrap round the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Volition is the power of choosing for oneself, the faculty of free will.

clue.text: Yank wearing a short coat

parts.note: to yank is to pull sharply, to jerk
someone wearing a coat is in it

explanation.surface: An American dressed in a short jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' suggests an American, but it is the verb meaning pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a sleeveless close-fitting jacket, historically of leather.

clue.text: Confession from a fellow who's smothered his wife (almost)

indicators.note: who's smothered means the college fellow surrounds the wife

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

indicators.note: almost means the word for his wife loses its last letter

parts.note: missis is an informal word for a man's wife

explanation.surface: A man owns up to having suffocated his wife, or nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last S from the wife; 'who's smothered' then wraps the university fellow round her, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is an acknowledgement of guilt or fact, the act of owning up.

clue.text: How Chinese might describe penniless chap

indicators.note: this plays on the old stereotype of Chinese speakers saying an L sound where English has R

parts.note: penniless means broke

explanation.surface: A Chinese speaker describing a man who has no money.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue relies on a dated stereotype: the R in BROKE becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloke is informal British slang for a man or fellow.

clue.text: Increase the wealth of Henri Christophe to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Making a Haitian king richer, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: Henri Christophe was a king of Haiti; the answer straddles his two names.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich someone is to make them richer, adding to their fortune.

clue.text: Control girl's credit

parts.note: Joy is a girl's name, with the possessive giving S
on tick means on credit, in British slang

explanation.surface: Managing a young woman's credit.
explanation.walkthrough: TICK is British slang for credit, as in buying 'on tick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A joystick is the lever used to steer an aircraft or a computer game, a control device.

clue.text: One may set out to be a farmer

indicators.note: set out means the letters are laid out afresh in another order

explanation.surface: Someone setting off to become a farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges ONEMAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeoman was a man who owned and worked his own small piece of land.

clue.text: Prompt willing man to cheat in race

parts.note: on means willing, as in 'I'm on'

indicators.note: in means the man and the cheating go inside the race

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
he refers to a man
to do someone is to cheat them

explanation.surface: Urging a keen man to cheat during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts HEDO inside TT. 'Prompt' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exactly on time is being punctual.

clue.text: Supplier of milk and chips to a Scots lad

parts.note: fries are chips, potato strips fried
Ian is the Scottish form of John

explanation.surface: Milk and chips being given to a Scottish boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Friesian is a black-and-white breed of dairy cow.

clue.text: Tap 'auls a litte water

parts.note: hauls means heaves; with the dropped H of Cockney speech it becomes eaves
a drop is a little water

explanation.surface: Someone hauling a small amount of water from a tap.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe marks a dropped H, so HEAVES loses its H. 'Tap' is the verb, as in tapping a phone line.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap a phone is to listen in secretly, which is what an eavesdropper does.

clue.text: Escape involving an opening over the door

indicators.note: involving means the escape surrounds the next word

parts.note: flight is an escape, as in fleeing

explanation.surface: Getting away through a gap above a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' wraps the escape round 'an'; 'opening' looks like a start but is a gap or window.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanlight is a window, often semicircular, set above a doorway.

clue.text: Physical fellow, about 28

parts.note: a mate is a fellow or companion

indicators.note: about means the word for a resting place is turned round

parts.note: 28 across is a resting place, and a lair is an animal's resting place

explanation.surface: A bodily man near some other clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 refers to 28 across, a resting place; 'about' reverses LAIR to RIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Material means relating to matter rather than spirit, that is, bodily or concrete.

clue.text: 1/3 of ice-creams end up producing pollution

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the pieces read from bottom to top
a third of the nine letters of ice-creams, here the final three

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A third of some ice-creams finishes as pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: '1/3 of' takes AMS, the last third of ICECREAMS; 'end' gives AIM; 'up' reverses AMSAIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a noxious vapour, the foul air once blamed for disease.

clue.text: Approach a meeting place

parts.note: a venue is a place where people meet

explanation.surface: Getting near a place to meet.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a way towards something, as in an avenue of enquiry or a tree-lined drive.

clue.text: After cooking, send roe back

indicators.note: after cooking means the letters are mixed up like ingredients

explanation.surface: Fish eggs returned after being cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a direction for the roe but is the definition, meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a plan is to support it, as when giving it an endorsement.

clue.text: Move easily embracing girl ready to be won over

indicators.note: embracing means the stroll wraps round the girl

parts.note: to amble is to walk at an easy pace
Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Walking along hugging a girl who is open to persuasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' wraps the leisurely walk round the girl's name; 'Move easily' looks like the definition but is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenable means open to persuasion, readily responsive.

clue.text: A pound I have charged

parts.note: L stands for the pound, from Latin libra
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone saying they have been charged a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' looks like billing but means electrically live.
explanation.definitionFit: A live wire is electrically charged.

clue.text: Mount dances, prancing about

indicators.note: prancing about means the letters jump into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A horse rearing and dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' suggests a horse, but it is a verb meaning climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount is to climb up, go upwards.

clue.text: Run over

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a run not scored off the bat is a bonus to the batting side, and over means additional or more than needed.

clue.text: Before long chapter will abandon one of its members

indicators.note: will abandon means the letter for chapter leaves the member's title

parts.note: a canon is a member of a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: A church chapter is about to lose a member.
explanation.walkthrough: A cathedral chapter is its governing body of clergy, the canons.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for soon, shortly.

clue.text: I wander about in New Zealand

indicators.note: about means the word for wander is turned round

parts.note: to roam is to wander

explanation.surface: A traveller roaming around New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed wander comes first in the answer even though I is printed first; 'about' turns ROAM to MAOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the indigenous Polynesian people of that country, so the word describes its first inhabitants.

clue.text: Goddess runs after information, a source of power

indicators.note: after means the goddess and runs come behind information

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Erato is the Greek muse of love poetry
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A goddess chases information and a supply of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information; ERATO is one of the Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: A generator is a machine that produces electricity.

clue.text: Order carpet and single bed, perhaps

indicators.note: order means the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Buying a carpet and a single bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' rearranges CARPET and SINGLE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed is one example of somewhere to lie down and repose; the question mark-like 'perhaps' marks an example.
